strategies.desc: Precompute all 7 intermediate masks and coverage counts once before any collectives, then perform 8 all-reduces back-to-back on masked buffers, deferring all division operations until the very end. Still requires 8 all-reduce dispatches but eliminates redundant mask recomputation across iterations and may enable better compiler fusion of the scaling operations. Trades memory (storing masks) for reduced compute overhead between dispatches.

strategies.name: Block-Wise Reduce-Scatter then All-Gather
strategies.desc: Restructure the dependent chain as a reduce-scatter phase (each rank owns specific blocks and accumulates only those) followed by an all-gather to broadcast results. Requires 2*7=14 or fewer dispatches depending on whether block assignment allows hierarchical aggregation, but each dispatch operates on smaller payloads (subsets of blocks). Exploits the block structure to reduce effective bandwidth per operation.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc: Leverage the 224-rank scale by organizing as intra-node (assuming multi-node deployment) and inter-node reductions, performing local node-level all-reduces first, then a global leader-based reduction, then broadcast back. Approximately 3*8=24 dispatches but with 224/num_nodes smaller participant sets for local operations, reducing bisection bandwidth pressure. Optimizes for network topology at the cost of additional dispatch overhead.

Split each of the 8 dependent stages into smaller independent sub-operations where possible (e.g., different block groups that don't interfere), issuing multiple concurrent all-reduce calls to overlap communication across non-conflicting blocks.
